source.text: Ἐὰν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής·

records.literal_gloss: If I testify about myself, the testimony of me not is true;

en.L: If I am testifying about {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony is not true.
en.B: If I testify on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own behalf, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony is not true.
en.R: If I am the only witness speaking about {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimony does not count as true.

es.L: Si yo doy testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, mi testimonio no es verdadero.
es.B: Si yo testifico a mi propio favor, mi testimonio no es verdadero.
es.R: Si yo fuera el único que habla a mi favor, mi testimonio no se podría tomar como verdadero.

sw.L: Ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} si wa kweli.
sw.B: Nikitoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, ushuhuda huo si kweli.
sw.R: Ikiwa ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} peke {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ninayeshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} hauwezi kukubalika kuwa kweli.

decisions.choice: true: valid as evidence, able to stand in a court
alternatives: true as opposed to false, as if Jesus were admitting that he lies
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks in the terms of a court. The law of Moses lets a charge stand only on the evidence of two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15; compare 17:6; Numbers 35:30), so a person's word about himself, standing alone, does not settle a case. Jesus grants the rule and goes on to name the witnesses who stand with him. In 8:13-14 his opponents turn the rule against him, and he answers that his testimony is true even about himself, because he knows where he came from; there "true" means truthful, and he again names the Father as the second witness (8:17-18). The two sayings do not conflict: one is about what counts as evidence, the other about whether he speaks the truth.

decisions.choice: testify, testimony: the language of a trial, which runs through the rest of the chapter
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charges of 5:16-18 as if in court, calling his witnesses one by one: John (5:33-35), the works the Father gave him (5:36), the Father himself (5:37) and the Scriptures (5:39); then he names Moses as the one who accuses his hearers (5:45). The verb and the noun for testifying occur eleven times in 5:31-39.

decisions.choice: testify ... testimony at every level
decisions.reason: The same pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, as in 1:7 and 3:11, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses. Readable uses "witness" only for the person who testifies.

decisions.choice: on my own behalf
decisions.reason: In a court, someone who testifies about himself speaks for his own case; Balanced says so plainly (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the only witness ... does not count as true
alternatives: If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the legal point (meaning decision m1), so that Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying.

decisions.choice: dar testimonio, testimonio
decisions.reason: The same pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, as in 1:7 and 3:11, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el único que habla a mi favor ... no se podría tomar como verdadero
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out the legal point (meaning decision m1), so Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying. Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting.

source.text: ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμοῦ, καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἣν μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Another is the [one] testifying about me, and I know that true is the testimony which he testifies about me.

en.L: Another is the one who testifies about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I know that the testimony which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} testifies about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true.
en.B: Someone else is testifying about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I know that the testimony {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true.
en.R: But there is another who testifies about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: the Father. And I know that what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true.

es.L: Otro es el que da testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y sé que es verdadero el testimonio que da acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Hay otro que da testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y sé que el testimonio que da de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} es verdadero.
es.R: Pero hay otro que da testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}: el Padre. Y sé que lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} es verdad.

sw.L: Mwingine ndiye anayeshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, nami najua kwamba ushuhuda anaoutoa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni wa kweli.
sw.B: Kuna mwingine anayeshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, nami najua kwamba ushuhuda anaotoa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni kweli.
sw.R: Lakini yuko mwingine anayenishuhudia: Baba. Nami najua kwamba anachosema juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni kweli.

decisions.choice: another: the Father
decisions.reason: John is named in the next verse, and some have taken him to be the other witness. But Jesus goes on to say that he does not accept testimony from a human being (5:34), that he has testimony greater than John's (5:36), and that the Father who sent him has testified about him (5:37). In 8:18 he says it outright: the Father who sent him testifies about him. The present tense "testifies" and Jesus's "I know" fit the Father best.

decisions.choice: the second witness the law requires
decisions.reason: With the Father beside him, Jesus is not a lone witness, and the rule of two witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15) is met, as he says again in 8:17-18.

decisions.choice: But ... : the Father
alternatives: Another is the one who testifies about me
decisions.reason: Readable names the other witness (meaning decision m1) and adds "But" to mark the turn from verse 31.

decisions.choice: the testimony he gives
decisions.reason: Balanced avoids repeating the same root twice in one phrase.

decisions.choice: Pero ...: el Padre
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the other witness (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάννην, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκε τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth;

en.L: You yourselves have sent [messengers] to John, and he has testified to the truth.
en.B: You yourselves sent messengers to John, and he has testified to the truth.
en.R: You sent messengers to ask John questions, and he testified to the truth.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes han enviado|Vosotros habéis enviado}} [mensajeros] a Juan, y él ha dado testimonio de la verdad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos enviaron|Vosotros mismos enviasteis}} mensajeros a Juan, y él ha dado testimonio de la verdad.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes enviaron|Vosotros enviasteis}} mensajeros a hacerle preguntas a Juan, y él dio testimonio de la verdad.

sw.L: Ninyi mmetuma [wajumbe] kwa Yohana, naye ametoa ushuhuda kwa ile kweli.
sw.B: Ninyi wenyewe mlipeleka wajumbe kwa Yohana, naye ametoa ushuhuda kwa ajili ya kweli.
sw.R: Mlituma wajumbe kumwuliza Yohana maswali, naye akaishuhudia kweli.

decisions.choice: the delegation sent from Jerusalem to question John (1:19-28)
decisions.reason: The Jewish authorities in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask John who he was (1:19, 24). He told them he was not the Christ and pointed to the one coming after him (1:20, 26-27); the next day he called Jesus the Lamb of God (1:29). Jesus is speaking to the same authorities (5:16-18), and the pronoun "you" is emphatic: you yourselves asked for John's testimony.

decisions.choice: the truth: the truth about who Jesus is
decisions.reason: John's testimony was about Jesus (1:15, 29-34). The perfect tense "has testified" means that his testimony still stands, though John's own work is over (5:35).

decisions.choice: [messengers] (L); messengers (B); messengers to ask John questions (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object of "sent" unstated; each level says who was sent (meaning decision m1), Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: You yourselves
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: [mensajeros] (L); mensajeros (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the Greek leaves the object of "sent" unstated (meaning decision m1). "Él" here is John and has no setting.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: But I not from a human the testimony receive, but these things I say so that you may be saved.

en.L: But I do not receive [my] testimony from {{gender:a human being|man}}; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
en.B: Yet I do not accept testimony from {{gender:a human being|man}}; I say these things so that you may be saved.
en.R: I do not depend on testimony from {{gender:people|men}}. I am telling you about John so that you can be saved.

es.L: Pero yo no recibo [mi] testimonio de {{gender:un ser humano|hombre}}, sino que digo estas cosas para que {{plural_you:ustedes sean salvos|vosotros seáis salvos}}.
es.B: Pero yo no acepto el testimonio de {{gender:ningún ser humano|ningún hombre}}; digo estas cosas para que {{plural_you:ustedes sean salvos|vosotros seáis salvos}}.
es.R: Yo no dependo del testimonio de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} hablo de Juan para que {{plural_you:ustedes puedan|vosotros podáis}} ser salvos.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sipokei ushuhuda kutoka kwa mwanadamu; badala yake ninasema mambo haya ili ninyi mwokolewe.
sw.B: Lakini sipokei ushuhuda kutoka kwa mwanadamu; nasema haya ili mpate kuokolewa.
sw.R: Sitegemei ushuhuda wa watu. Nawaambia habari za Yohana ili mpate kuokolewa.

decisions.choice: Jesus does not depend on human testimony; he mentions John for his hearers' sake
alternatives: Jesus rejects John's testimony as false
decisions.reason: John's testimony was true (5:33), but Jesus's claim does not rest on any human witness; the one who vouches for him is the Father (5:32, 37). The article ("the testimony") points to the testimony that counts for him. He reminds his hearers of John because they once welcomed John (5:35), and John's word could still lead them to him.

decisions.choice: be saved: rescued from judgment and given life
decisions.reason: As in 3:17, and in the terms of this chapter: the one who hears Jesus's word and believes the one who sent him has eternal life and does not come into judgment (5:24).

decisions.choice: [my]
decisions.reason: The Greek article points to the testimony Jesus relies on (meaning decision m1); Literal supplies "my" in brackets.

decisions.choice: accept (B); depend on (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means receive or accept. It recurs through the passage: Jesus does not accept glory from people (5:41), they do not accept him (5:43), and they accept glory from one another (5:44). Balanced says "accept" each time and Literal "receive" each time, so the thread stays visible.

decisions.choice: about John
decisions.reason: "These things" refers to what Jesus has just said about John's testimony; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: a human being (L, B); people (R), under the gender setting
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, not a male; the traditional "man" is the alternative, as in 2:25.

decisions.choice: {{gender:un ser humano|hombre}} (L); {{gender:ningún ser humano|ningún hombre}} (B); {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} (R)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, not a male (meaning decision m1); inclusive default, traditional one tap away.

decisions.choice: de Juan
decisions.reason: As in English: "estas cosas" refers to what Jesus has just said about John.

source.text: ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: That one was the lamp the [one] burning and shining, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in the light of him;

en.L: That one was the lamp that was burning and shining, and you were willing for a while to rejoice in his light.
en.B: John was the lamp that burned and shone, and for a little while you were glad to rejoice in his light.
en.R: John was like a lamp that was lit and shining. For a short time you were happy to enjoy his light.

es.L: Aquel era la lámpara que ardía y alumbraba, y {{plural_you:ustedes quisieron regocijarse|vosotros quisisteis regocijaros}} por un tiempo en su luz.
es.B: Juan era la lámpara que ardía y alumbraba, y por un poco de tiempo {{plural_you:ustedes quisieron alegrarse|vosotros quisisteis alegraros}} con su luz.
es.R: Juan era como una lámpara encendida que alumbraba. Por un tiempo {{plural_you:ustedes estuvieron|vosotros estuvisteis}} contentos de disfrutar de su luz.

sw.L: Yule alikuwa ndiye taa inayowaka na kumulika, nanyi mlikuwa tayari kwa kitambo kushangilia katika nuru yake.
sw.B: Yohana alikuwa taa iliyowaka na kung'aa, na kwa muda mfupi mlifurahi kushangilia katika nuru yake.
sw.R: Yohana alikuwa kama taa iliyowashwa na kung'aa. Kwa muda mfupi mlifurahi kufaidi nuru yake.

decisions.choice: a lamp, not the light
decisions.reason: John was not the light but came to testify about the light (1:8); Jesus is the light (1:9; 8:12). A lamp shines, but it has to be lit, and it burns down. The article may point to a familiar picture: in Psalm 132:17 God says he has prepared a lamp for his anointed one.

decisions.choice: was: John's work is over
decisions.reason: The past tense speaks of John's witness as finished. By this time he may have been put in prison or put to death; 3:24 notes that at an earlier point he had not yet been imprisoned.

decisions.choice: for an hour: for a short time
alternatives: for the length of an hour
decisions.reason: The phrase is an ordinary way of saying "for a while" (2 Corinthians 7:8; Galatians 2:5; Philemon 15). It is not the "hour" of Jesus's appointed time.

decisions.choice: you were willing to rejoice: their gladness in John was real but short-lived
decisions.reason: The verb for rejoicing means great gladness, even exultation. The people delighted in John for a while, but their delight did not carry them to the one he pointed to (5:33-34, 40).

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "that one"; Balanced and Readable name John, so that no reader takes it to be Jesus.

decisions.choice: for a while (L); for a little while (B); for a short time (R)
decisions.reason: "For an hour" would sound like a clock time (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: like a lamp
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison so that young readers do not take it literally.

decisions.choice: Juan
decisions.reason: As in English: the Greek has only "aquel"; Balanced and Readable name John, so no reader takes it to be Jesus.

decisions.choice: por un tiempo / por un poco de tiempo
decisions.reason: "Por una hora" would sound like a clock time (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔχω τὴν μαρτυρίαν μείζω τοῦ Ἰωάννου, τὰ γὰρ ἔργα ἃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τελειώσω αὐτά, αὐτὰ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιῶ, μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ὁ πατήρ με ἀπέσταλκεν, καὶ ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ ἐκεῖνος μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But I have the testimony greater than of John; for the works which has given to me the Father so that I may complete them, the very works which I do, testify about me that the Father me has sent. \v 37 And the having-sent me Father, that one has testified about me.

en.L: But I have the testimony greater than John's; for the works that the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so that I may complete them, the very works that I do, testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But I have a testimony greater than John's. The works the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to bring to completion, the works themselves that I am doing, testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: they show that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: But I have testimony that is greater than John's. The Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} works to do and to finish. These works that I am doing testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They show that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero yo tengo un testimonio mayor que el de Juan; porque las obras que el Padre me ha dado para que las lleve a cabo, las mismas obras que hago, dan testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} de que el Padre me ha enviado. \v 37 Y el Padre que me envió, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha dado testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Pero yo tengo un testimonio mayor que el de Juan. Las obras que el Padre me ha encargado llevar a término, las mismas obras que estoy haciendo, dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}: muestran que el Padre me ha enviado. \v 37 Y el Padre que me envió ha dado testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo.
es.R: Pero yo tengo un testimonio más grande que el de Juan. El Padre me ha dado obras para hacer y terminar. Estas obras que estoy haciendo dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Muestran que el Padre me ha enviado. \v 37 Y el Padre que me envió ha dado testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninao ushuhuda mkubwa zaidi kuliko wa Yohana; kwa maana kazi ambazo Baba amenikabidhi ili nizitimize, kazi hizo hizo ninazozifanya, zinatoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwamba Baba ndiye aliyenituma. \v 37 Na Baba aliyenituma, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} amenishuhudia.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nina ushuhuda ulio mkuu kuliko wa Yohana. Kazi Baba alizonipa nizikamilishe, kazi zenyewe ninazozifanya, zinashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}: zinaonyesha kwamba Baba amenituma. \v 37 Na Baba aliyenituma amenishuhudia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nina ushuhuda mkuu kuliko wa Yohana. Baba amenipa kazi za kufanya na kuzimaliza. Kazi hizi ninazozifanya zinanishuhudia. Zinaonyesha kwamba Baba amenituma. \v 37 Na Baba aliyenituma ameshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.

decisions.choice: the works: all that the Father has given Jesus to do, his signs included
decisions.reason: Where the narrator and the crowds speak of "signs", Jesus speaks of the "works" the Father has given him (5:20; 9:3-4; 10:25, 37-38; 14:10-11). They include the healing at the pool (5:17) and the greater works of giving life and judging (5:20-22). Because the Father is at work in them, they testify that he sent Jesus.

decisions.choice: complete: carry the Father's work through to its end
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 4:34 and 17:4; from the cross Jesus says "It is finished" (19:30), a word from the same root.

decisions.choice: the Father's testimony: left open, as the text leaves it
alternatives: what God told John about the Spirit coming down on Jesus (1:33)
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says that the Father has given his testimony and that it stands. Jesus does not say how. It may be the works through which the Father acts (5:36), the Scriptures that testify about Jesus (5:39), or the sign God gave John when the Spirit came down on Jesus (1:32-34). Verse 38 adds that his hearers do not receive it, because his word does not remain in them.

decisions.choice: he: emphatic, the Father himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is not needed for the sense; it stresses the person: the Father himself, not a lesser witness.

decisions.choice: the works ... testify about me: they show that
alternatives: testify about me that the Father has sent me
decisions.reason: Balanced separates the testimony of the works from what it shows, so that the long Greek clause reads clearly.

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: Shows the emphasis of meaning decision m4.

decisions.choice: The Father has given me works to do and to finish. These works ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence into short ones.

decisions.choice: dan testimonio de mí: muestran que
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced separates the testimony of the works from what it shows.

decisions.choice: él (L); él mismo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m4). It refers to the Father, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: οὔτε φωνὴν αὐτοῦ πώποτε ἀκηκόατε οὔτε εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἑωράκατε, καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ὑμῖν μένοντα, ὅτι ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος τούτῳ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε.

records.literal_gloss: Neither voice of him ever have you heard nor form of him have you seen, \v 38 and the word of him not you have in you remaining, because whom sent that one, this one you not believe.

en.L: Neither have you ever heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, nor have you seen {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} form, \v 38 and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word you do not have remaining in you, because the one whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you do not believe.
en.B: Not once have you heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice or seen {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} form. \v 38 And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word does not remain in you, since you do not believe the very one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent.
en.R: You have never heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice. You have never seen what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looks like. \v 38 And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word does not remain in you. That is clear, because you do not believe the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent.

es.L: Nunca {{plural_you:han oído|habéis oído}} su voz ni {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} su aspecto, \v 38 ni {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} su palabra permaneciendo en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque al que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envió, a ese no le {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}.
es.B: Nunca {{plural_you:han oído|habéis oído}} su voz ni {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} su aspecto. \v 38 Y su palabra no permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} al que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envió.
es.R: Nunca {{plural_you:han oído|habéis oído}} su voz. Nunca {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} cómo es. \v 38 Y su palabra no permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Eso se ve claramente, porque no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} al que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envió.

sw.L: Hamjapata kamwe kuisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wala hamjauona umbo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 38 na hamna neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} linalokaa ndani yenu, kwa sababu yule ambaye {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alimtuma, huyo ninyi hammwamini.
sw.B: Hamjawahi kuisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} wala kuuona umbo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. \v 38 Na neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} halikai ndani yenu, kwa kuwa hammwamini yule hasa aliyemtuma.
sw.R: Hamjawahi kamwe kuisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Hamjawahi kuona jinsi alivyo. \v 38 Na neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} halikai ndani yenu. Hilo liko wazi, kwa sababu hammwamini yule aliyemtuma.

decisions.choice: a contrast with Israel at Sinai
alternatives: a plain statement that no one has seen God (1:18)
decisions.reason: At Sinai Israel heard the voice of God out of the fire, though they saw no form (Deuteronomy 4:12, 15, 33), and God said that Moses sees the form of the LORD (Numbers 12:8). Jesus's hearers claim that heritage, yet they have not heard God's voice: they do not recognize it in the one he sent. The words may instead restate that no one has ever seen God except the Son (1:18; 6:46), so that the Father's testimony reaches people only through him. Both readings lead to the point of verse 38.

decisions.choice: remain: stay and take root
decisions.reason: God's word has no lasting home in them. Jesus uses the same verb when he speaks of his words remaining in his disciples (15:7; compare 1 John 2:14).

decisions.choice: because: their unbelief shows that God's word is not in them
alternatives: their unbelief is the cause of God's word not remaining in them
decisions.reason: Unbelief here is the evidence: if God's word lived in them, they would recognize the one God sent.

decisions.choice: remain
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: "remain" in this sense, not the older "abide".

decisions.choice: the very one
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun near the end of the Greek sentence.

decisions.choice: That is clear, because
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that their unbelief is the sign (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: permanecer
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this verb in its weighty sense, as in 1:32-33 and 3:36.

decisions.choice: Eso se ve claramente, porque
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable makes plain that their unbelief is the sign (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Ἐραυνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς δοκεῖτε ἐν αὐταῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχειν· καὶ ἐκεῖναί εἰσιν αἱ μαρτυροῦσαι περὶ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: You search the Scriptures, because you think in them life eternal to have; and those are the [ones] testifying about me;

en.L: You search the Scriptures, because you think you have eternal life in them; and those are the [ones] testifying about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: You pore over the Scriptures, since you think that eternal life is to be found in them; and they are the ones that testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: You study the Scriptures carefully, because you think that in them you have eternal life, the life of the age to come. And the Scriptures themselves testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Escudriñan|Escudriñáis}} las Escrituras, porque {{plural_you:ustedes piensan|vosotros pensáis}} tener en ellas vida eterna; y ellas son las que dan testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Estudian a fondo|Estudiáis a fondo}} las Escrituras, porque {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que en ellas se encuentra la vida eterna; y son ellas las que dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Estudian|Estudiáis}} las Escrituras con cuidado, porque {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que en ellas {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero. Y las mismas Escrituras dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Mnayachunguza Maandiko, kwa kuwa ninyi mnadhani kwamba ndani yake mtapata kuwa na uzima wa milele; nayo ndiyo yanayotoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Mnayasoma Maandiko kwa bidii, kwa kuwa mnadhani kwamba uzima wa milele unapatikana ndani yake; na hayo ndiyo yanayoshuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.
sw.R: Mnajifunza Maandiko kwa makini, kwa sababu mnadhani kwamba ndani yake mna uzima wa milele, uzima wa nyakati zijazo. Na Maandiko yenyewe yanashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.

decisions.choice: You search: a statement
decisions.reason: The Greek form can be either. Jesus goes on to give the reason they search ("because you think ...") and to say that they still will not come to him (5:40); both fit a statement about what they already do. As a command, the words would call them to search and find that the Scriptures point to him. A footnote gives the command.

decisions.choice: you think that in them you have eternal life: the Law as the way of life
decisions.reason: The Law itself promised life to those who keep it (Leviticus 18:5; Deuteronomy 30:15-20; 32:47). Jesus does not deny that the Scriptures speak of life; he says that they point to him, the one who gives it (5:21, 24-26).

decisions.choice: the Scriptures: the Jewish Scriptures, which Christians call the Old Testament
decisions.reason: The New Testament had not yet been written; Jesus means the Law, the Prophets and the other writings his hearers read.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, God's own life, which begins now
decisions.reason: Key term, as in 3:15-16 and 5:24.

decisions.choice: pore over (B); study ... carefully (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to search or examine closely; Balanced and Readable use words that suggest close study of a text.

decisions.choice: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage, as the book-wide choice for John allows (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Escudriñan / Escudriñáis: a statement
decisions.reason: The Greek form can be a statement or a command; Spanish must choose, and the vosotros command "Escudriñad" is the familiar older wording. Every level follows meaning decision m1, whose footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: estudian a fondo (B); estudian con cuidado (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: words that suggest close study of a text.

decisions.choice: la vida del mundo venidero
decisions.reason: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage (meaning decision m4).

source.text: καὶ οὐ θέλετε ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχητε.

records.literal_gloss: and not you are willing to come to me so that life you may have.

en.L: And you are not willing to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so that you may have life.
en.B: But you do not want to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so that you can have life.
en.R: But you do not want to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so that you can have that life.

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para tener vida.
es.B: Pero no {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para tener vida.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para tener esa vida.

sw.L: Na hampendi kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} ili mwe na uzima.
sw.B: Lakini hamtaki kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} ili mpate uzima.
sw.R: Lakini hamtaki kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} ili mpate uzima huo.

decisions.choice: and: with the force of "and yet"
decisions.reason: The Scriptures testify about Jesus, and yet his hearers will not come to him. The plain "and" carries the contrast.

decisions.choice: not willing: they will not, not that they cannot
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of what someone wants or chooses. Jesus asked the man at the pool the same question with the same verb: "Do you want to be made well?" (5:6).

decisions.choice: come to me: put their trust in him
decisions.reason: In John, coming to Jesus and believing in him go together (6:35; 7:37-38).

decisions.choice: But ... do not want
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the contrast (meaning decision m1) and use the everyday verb.

decisions.choice: Pero ... no quieren
decisions.reason: As in English: states the contrast (meaning decision m1). "Querer" is the same verb as Jesus's question at the pool, "¿Quieres quedar sano?" (5:6; meaning decision m2).

source.text: δόξαν παρὰ ἀνθρώπων οὐ λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ἔγνωκα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Glory from humans not I receive, \v 42 but I have known you that the love of the God not you have in yourselves.

en.L: Glory from {{gender:people|men}} I do not receive, \v 42 but I know you, that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.
en.B: Glory from {{gender:people|men}} is not something I accept. \v 42 But I know you, and there is no love for God in you.
en.R: I do not accept glory from {{gender:people|men}}. \v 42 But I know you. In your hearts you do not love God.

es.L: Gloria de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} no recibo, \v 42 sino que {{plural_you:los|os}} conozco, que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} el amor de Dios en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos.
es.B: La gloria que viene de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} no la acepto. \v 42 Pero {{plural_you:los|os}} conozco, y sé que no hay en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} amor a Dios.
es.R: Yo no acepto gloria de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}. \v 42 Pero {{plural_you:los|os}} conozco. {{plural_you:Ustedes no aman|Vosotros no amáis}} a Dios de corazón.

sw.L: Utukufu kutoka kwa watu sipokei, \v 42 lakini nawajua ninyi, kwamba upendo wa Mungu hamnao ndani yenu.
sw.B: Utukufu kutoka kwa watu si kitu ninachokikubali. \v 42 Lakini nawajua ninyi, na hamna upendo kwa Mungu ndani yenu.
sw.R: Sikubali utukufu kutoka kwa watu. \v 42 Lakini nawajua. Mioyoni mwenu hammpendi Mungu.

decisions.choice: glory: honor and approval given by people
alternatives: the divine glory seen in Jesus (1:14)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the honor people give one another, a common sense of it. Jesus does not depend on human approval any more than on human testimony (5:34). The same contrast between glory from people and glory from God returns in 5:44, 7:18 and 12:43.

decisions.choice: the love of God: their love for God
alternatives: the love that comes from God
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean God's love or love for God. The context is about where their hearts are turned: they accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from God (5:44). Israel's first command was to love the LORD with all the heart (Deuteronomy 6:5), and that love is what Jesus says is missing. The other senses are close: those who have God's love in them love him in return (1 John 4:19).

decisions.choice: I know you: Jesus knows their hearts
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means a settled knowledge. As in 2:24-25, Jesus knows what is in people; here he knows these hearers and says what is missing in them.

decisions.choice: love for God (B); you do not love God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase as it stands; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: Glory from people first
alternatives: I do not receive glory from people
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "glory" at the front, as the Greek does for emphasis.

decisions.choice: In your hearts
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday way of speaking about what is inside a person.

decisions.choice: amor a Dios (B); no aman a Dios (R); el amor de Dios (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase as it stands; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: People in general: inclusive default, traditional one tap away.

source.text: ἐγὼ ἐλήλυθα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρός μου καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετέ με· ἐὰν ἄλλος ἔλθῃ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ, ἐκεῖνον λήμψεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: I have come in the name of the Father of me, and not you receive me; if another comes in the name the own, that one you will receive.

en.L: I have come in the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you do not receive {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; if another comes in his own name, that one you will receive.
en.B: I have come in the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, yet you do not accept {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Should someone else come in his own name, him you will accept.
en.R: I have come with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's authority, but you do not accept {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If someone else comes on his own authority, you will accept him.

es.L: Yo he venido en el nombre de mi Padre, y no me {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}}; si otro viene en su propio nombre, a ese lo {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}}.
es.B: Yo he venido en nombre de mi Padre, y no me {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}}. Si otro viniera en su propio nombre, a ese sí lo {{plural_you:aceptarían|aceptaríais}}.
es.R: Yo he venido con la autoridad de mi Padre, pero no me {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}}. Si viene otro con su propia autoridad, a ese sí lo {{plural_you:aceptarán|aceptaréis}}.

sw.L: Nimekuja katika jina la Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na hamnipokei; ikiwa mwingine atakuja katika jina lake mwenyewe, yule mtampokea.
sw.B: Nimekuja kwa jina la Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, lakini hamnipokei. Mtu mwingine akija kwa jina lake mwenyewe, mtampokea huyo.
sw.R: Nimekuja na mamlaka ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, lakini hamnikubali. Mtu mwingine akija kwa mamlaka yake mwenyewe, mtamkubali.

decisions.choice: in the name of: as his representative, with his authority
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to come as their envoy, carrying their authority (Deuteronomy 18:19; Psalm 118:26, which the crowd sings in 12:13). The other comes in his own name: no one has sent him.

decisions.choice: another: anyone who comes on his own authority
decisions.reason: Jesus names no one. The point is the contrast: they reject the one God sent and would welcome one whom no one sent. One who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory (7:18), and that suits hearers who accept glory from one another (5:44).

decisions.choice: receive: welcome, accept as what he claims to be
decisions.reason: As in 1:11-12: his own did not receive him, but to all who received him he gave the right to become children of God.

decisions.choice: with my Father's authority ... on his own authority
alternatives: in my Father's name ... in his own name
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Should someone else come ..., him you will accept
alternatives: If someone else comes ..., you will accept him
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress the Greek puts on "that one" at the end of the sentence.

decisions.choice: his own name, him: no gender setting
decisions.reason: The words picture a man who sets himself up against Jesus; the Greek pronoun is masculine, and the saying is kept as it stands, as with the prophet in 4:44.

decisions.choice: con la autoridad de mi Padre ... con su propia autoridad
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m1). The "otro" is kept as it stands, with no gender setting.

source.text: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι, δόξαν παρ’ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: How are able you to believe, glory from one another receiving, and the glory the [one] from the only God not you seek?

en.L: How are you able to believe, receiving glory from one another, and the glory that [comes] from the only God you do not seek?
en.B: How could you believe? You accept glory from one another, while the glory that comes from the only God is something you do not seek.
en.R: You accept glory from each other, but you do not look for the glory that comes from the only God. So how can you believe?

es.L: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:pueden ustedes|podéis vosotros}} creer, recibiendo gloria unos de otros, y la gloria que [viene] del único Dios no {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?
es.B: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} creer? {{plural_you:Aceptan|Aceptáis}} gloria unos de otros, mientras que la gloria que viene del único Dios no la {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes aceptan|Vosotros aceptáis}} gloria unos de otros, pero no {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} la gloria que viene del único Dios. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} creer?

sw.L: Ninyi mnawezaje kuamini, mkipokea utukufu kutoka kwa mtu na mwenzake, nao utukufu ulio kutoka kwa Mungu pekee hamuutafuti?
sw.B: Mnawezaje kuamini? Mnapokea utukufu kutoka kwa kila mmoja wenu, lakini utukufu unaotoka kwa Mungu pekee hamuutafuti.
sw.R: Mnapokea utukufu kutoka kwa kila mmoja wenu, lakini hamuutafuti utukufu unaotoka kwa Mungu pekee. Basi mnawezaje kuamini?

decisions.choice: receiving glory: the reason they cannot believe
alternatives: only a description alongside the question
decisions.reason: The participle gives the cause: people who live for one another's approval cannot accept the one God sent, whom others reject (compare 12:42-43).

decisions.choice: glory: honor and approval
decisions.reason: The same sense as in 5:41: the honor they give one another against the honor that comes from God.

decisions.choice: from the only God (SBLGNT)
alternatives: from the only one (some early manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them the papyri P66 and P75 and Codex Vaticanus, lack the word for God and read "the glory from the only one"; the sense is the same, since the only one is God. The word may have dropped out because, written in the usual short form, it looked very like the ending of the word before it. A reviewer should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the only God: the confession that God is one
decisions.reason: Israel confessed that the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), and Jesus calls the Father "the only true God" (17:3). His hearers honor the one God in word, yet they seek honor from one another.

decisions.choice: How could you believe? You accept ...
alternatives: How can you believe, when you accept ...?
decisions.reason: Balanced asks the question first and then gives the reason as a statement, which keeps the long sentence clear.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states what they do and then asks the question, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: the question first (B) or last (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps the long sentence clear.

source.text: μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα· ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε.

records.literal_gloss: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; there is the [one] accusing you, Moses, in whom you have hoped.

en.L: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; the one who accuses you is Moses, in whom you have hoped.
en.B: Do not imagine that I will be the one to accuse you before the Father. You already have an accuser: Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
en.R: Do not think that I am the one who will accuse you to the Father. Moses is the one who accuses you, the very Moses you have put your hope in.

es.L: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} acusaré ante el Padre; el que {{plural_you:los|os}} acusa es Moisés, en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se imaginen|os imaginéis}} que seré yo quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acuse ante el Padre. Ya {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acuse: Moisés, en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que yo soy el que {{plural_you:los|os}} va a acusar ante el Padre. Moisés es el que {{plural_you:los|os}} acusa, el mismo Moisés en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.

sw.L: Msifikiri kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitawashtaki kwa Baba; mshtaki wenu ni Musa, yule ambaye mmeweka tumaini lenu kwake.
sw.B: Msidhani kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye nitakayewashtaki mbele ya Baba. Tayari mnaye mshtaki: Musa, mliyemwekea tumaini lenu.
sw.R: Msifikiri kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye nitakayewashtaki kwa Baba. Musa ndiye anayewashtaki, yule yule Musa mliyemtumainia.

decisions.choice: Moses accuses them through the Law he wrote
decisions.reason: Moses was remembered as the one who pleaded with God for Israel (Exodus 32:11-14, 30-32); here he is their accuser instead. Moses himself had the book of the Law placed beside the ark as a witness against the people (Deuteronomy 31:26): the Law they rely on testifies against those who do not listen to it.

decisions.choice: set your hope on Moses: relied on Moses and his Law for their standing with God
decisions.reason: They counted on being disciples of Moses (9:28-29) and keepers of his Law. The perfect tense describes a hope they have held and still hold.

decisions.choice: I: emphatic; it is not Jesus who will bring the charge
decisions.reason: The Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22, 27), yet Jesus says he will not need to accuse them; the pronoun stresses the contrast with Moses. Elsewhere he says he came not to judge the world but to save it (3:17; 12:47-48).

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: The present participle "the one accusing" describes an accuser already at work; Balanced says so.

decisions.choice: put your hope in
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes a settled hope; "put your hope in" says that more naturally than "have hoped".

decisions.choice: I will be the one to accuse (B); I am the one who will accuse (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: seré yo quien (B); yo soy el que (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Ya
decisions.reason: As in English: an accuser already at work.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί, περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν.

records.literal_gloss: For if you were believing Moses, you would believe me; for about me that one wrote.

en.L: For if you believed Moses, you would believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; for it was about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that he wrote.
en.B: If you really believed Moses, you would believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because what he wrote was about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: If you truly believed Moses, you would believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} too, because Moses wrote about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Porque si {{plural_you:creyeran|creyerais}} a Moisés, me {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; porque de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} escribió él.
es.B: Si de verdad {{plural_you:creyeran|creyerais}} a Moisés, me {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque lo que él escribió era acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Si de verdad {{plural_you:creyeran|creyerais}} a Moisés, también me {{plural_you:creerían|creeríais}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque Moisés escribió acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ikiwa mngekuwa mnamwamini Musa, mngekuwa mnaniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}; maana ni juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliandika yule.
sw.B: Kama kweli mngemwamini Musa, mngeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa sababu aliyoyaandika yalikuwa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Kama kweli mngemwamini Musa, mngeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} pia, kwa sababu Musa aliandika habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they do not really believe Moses
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the opposite of the if-clause: they do not believe Moses, and so they do not believe Jesus. Their hope in Moses (5:45) is not real belief in what he wrote.

decisions.choice: the writings of Moses as a whole point to Jesus
alternatives: one particular passage, such as the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-18)
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a passage. The books of Moses, Genesis to Deuteronomy, contain promises and patterns that John elsewhere connects with Jesus: Philip speaks of the one Moses wrote about in the Law (1:45); the crowds wonder whether Jesus is the Prophet (6:14; 7:40), the prophet like Moses whom God promised to raise up (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); and Jesus compares himself to the serpent Moses lifted up (3:14) and to the manna (6:31-35).

decisions.choice: believe someone: take that person's word as true
decisions.reason: With a person as its object in this form, the verb means to believe what the person says, not yet to "believe in" him. Jesus asks his hearers to trust his words as they claim to trust Moses's (5:47).

decisions.choice: really (B); truly (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that the condition is contrary to fact (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: de verdad
decisions.reason: As in English: shows that the condition is contrary to fact (meaning decision m1). "Creer a" + person, not "creer en" (m3); "él" is Moses.

source.text: εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασιν πιστεύσετε;

records.literal_gloss: But if the of that one writings not you believe, how the my words will you believe?

en.L: But if the writings of that one you do not believe, how will you believe {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words?"
en.B: But if you do not believe the writings of Moses, how will you ever believe {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spoken words?"
en.R: But you do not believe what Moses wrote. So how will you believe what I say?"

es.L: Pero si no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} los escritos de aquel, ¿cómo {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}} mis palabras?».
es.B: Pero si no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} lo que escribió Moisés, ¿cómo {{plural_you:van|vais}} a creer las palabras que yo digo?».
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} lo que escribió Moisés. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:van|vais}} a creer lo que yo digo?».

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa maandiko ya yule hamyaamini, mtayaaminije maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa hamyaamini maandiko ya Musa, mtayaaminije kamwe maneno ninayoyasema?"
sw.R: Lakini hamuamini alichoandika Musa. Basi mtaaminije ninachosema?"

decisions.choice: his writings and my words: what Moses wrote and what Jesus speaks
decisions.reason: Jesus sets the written word of Moses beside his own spoken words. His hearers honor the books of Moses as Scripture; if they do not believe what those books say, they will not believe the words of one standing in front of them, though his words are the Father's (3:34; 17:8).

decisions.choice: if: a condition taken as true
decisions.reason: After verse 46 the if-clause states what is actually the case: they do not believe what Moses wrote.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Names Moses, the one meant by "that one".

decisions.choice: spoken words
decisions.reason: Brings out the contrast between what is written and what is spoken (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: a statement instead of an if-clause
alternatives: But if you do not believe what Moses wrote
decisions.reason: Readable states as fact what the condition assumes (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Moisés
decisions.reason: As in English: names Moses, the one meant by "aquel". Balanced's "las palabras que yo digo" keeps the contrast between written and spoken (meaning decision m1). The speech that began in 5:19 closes here.
